current.text: He re-signed with Portland for 3 years and 44 million USD.
He is the backup center behind Donovan Clingan. Clingan is in the projected starting five.
He outplayed Clingan in the playoffs. The contract shows the team trusts him, but he is not expected to start over Clingan.
He is expected to be capped at 17 to 18 minutes a night and to sit about 16 back-to-backs.
A local Blazers analyst does not expect Clingan to play over 28 minutes, which leaves backup center minutes for him.
Most of his FG% value comes from twos. His 2P% jumped from 65 to 74, and the expert expects it to fall back to about 68.
At about 23 minutes a night he would be a draftable category-league player.
Portland has a new head coach, and minutes and usage are expected to swing from game to game across the rotation.
Portland has three back-to-backs in the fantasy playoffs. If he sits back-to-backs, he loses games in weeks 19 to 21.

durable.text: His blocks are a league outlier for his minutes. He adds a high FG% on low volume, few turnovers and solid rebounds.
He makes almost no threes and scores few points, even for a center.
His minutes and health are hard to trust.

note: He is ranked 202 on Yahoo and 165 on ESPN, both sites value him at 0 USD, and he was not drafted in our league last season. That puts him outside the 144 players we draft. His value is blocks (z +2.1 vs the pool), FG% and low turnovers on about 17 minutes, so he only fits a punt PTS build that needs blocks, and his 59.6 FT% last season is a small drag. Leave him on waivers at the draft. Pick him up if his minutes rise toward 23 or Clingan misses time, and watch whether his FG% holds near 70.
